articles.title: 2027 Social Security COLA: Every benefit that will increase and how much could you get?
articles.standfirst: The official increase isn't final yet, but current forecasts point to around 3.5 percent.
articles.summary: The official increase isn't final yet, but current forecasts point to around 3.5 percent.
articles.body:
Millions of Americans receiving Social Security or Supplemental Security Income could see higher monthly payments in 2027 as the annual cost of living adjustment takes effect.

AARP currently estimates the 2027 COLA at 3.5 percent, although the final figure won't be announced until October 14 after September inflation data is released.

The increase will apply across Social Security retirement, survivor and disability benefits, while SSI payments also rise through the annual COLA system.

How much could Social Security payments increase?

AARP says the average retired worker currently receives about $2,086 a month.

With a 3.5 percent COLA, that would increase by roughly $73, taking the average monthly payment to around $2,159.

Surviving spouses currently receive an average of about $1,933 per month. A 3.5 percent increase would add around $68, pushing the average payment to approximately $2,001.

SSDI recipients would also benefit.

AARP estimates that the average disabled worker receives $1,635 per month. Applying a 3.5 percent COLA would increase that by around $57, taking the average payment to roughly $1,692.

SSI payments will increase too

Supplemental Security Income is also adjusted through the same annual COLA mechanism.

The maximum federal SSI payment in 2026 is $994 per month for an individual and $1,491 for an eligible couple.

If the final 2027 COLA is 3.5 percent, those figures would rise to approximately $1,028 for an individual and around $1,543 for an eligible couple, although the official amounts won't be confirmed until the COLA is finalized.

When will the 2027 COLA be confirmed?

The Social Security Administration calculates COLA using third-quarter inflation measured by the CPI-W.

Yahoo Finance reports that the official increase is expected to be announced on October 14.

Any new COLA will begin affecting Social Security checks paid in January 2027, while SSI recipients typically receive their January payment at the end of December because January 1 is a federal holiday.

The important point is that 3.5 percent remains an estimate .

Your exact increase will depend on the final COLA and your existing benefit amount, but retirement, survivor, SSDI and SSI payments are all positioned to rise if inflation produces a positive adjustment.

articles.title: Five dead after Amazon plane crash causes major travel disruptions at Miami airport
articles.summary: Miami International Airport is facing major travel disruptions after an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway Sunday, Sept. 6, killing at least five people and sending five others to the hospital.
articles.body:
Miami International Airport is facing major travel disruptions after an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway Sunday, Sept. 6, killing at least five people and sending five others to the hospital.

Prime Air Flight 7598 crashed into multiple vehicles and burst into flames around 2 p.m., while emergency crews worked for hours to contain a fuel leak. As of Monday morning, the aircraft had not been moved, forcing the closure of two of the airport’s four runways.

The crash occurred during the busy Labor Day travel rush, with at least 55 flights cancelled and more than 100 delayed at Miami International Airport.

articles.title: Who is getting their SSDI payment tomorrow? Complete list of beneficiaries for deposit
articles.standfirst: Your birthday determines whether the next Social Security deposit is heading to your account
articles.summary: Your birthday determines whether the next Social Security deposit is heading to your account
articles.body:
The next September Social Security Disability Insurance payment is due Wednesday, with one specific group of beneficiaries first in line under the Social Security Administration ’s staggered monthly schedule.

People receiving SSDI whose birthdays fall between the 1st and 10th of any month are scheduled to receive their September payment on Wednesday, September 9.

That means the month someone was born doesn't affect this particular payment date. A beneficiary born on February 3, July 7 or November 10 would generally be included in the same group because Social Security bases the schedule on the day of the month.

The system divides most Social Security retirement and disability recipients into three groups.

Those born between the 1st and 10th are paid on the second Wednesday, birthdays from the 11th through 20th are paid on the third Wednesday, and those born from the 21st through 31st receive benefits on the fourth Wednesday.

Who should receive an SSDI payment on September 9?

Wednesday’s deposit applies to most SSDI beneficiaries who follow the regular birthday-based Social Security payment calendar and were born between the 1st and 10th.

The same scheduling system is also used for most people receiving Social Security retirement benefits.

Some beneficiaries who receive payments based on another person’s earnings record, including certain spouses and survivors, follow the birthday of the worker whose record provides the benefit rather than their own birthday.

Not every SSDI recipient will be waiting for Wednesday, however. People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 generally follow a different timetable and are normally paid on the third of the month.

Beneficiaries who receive both Supplemental Security Income and Social Security also typically receive their SSI payment on the first of the month and their Social Security benefit on the third.

Those September payments have therefore already been scheduled earlier in the month.

Two more September payment dates still coming

Beneficiaries who aren't part of the September 9 group may have to wait another week or two.

People whose birthdays fall between the 11th and 20th are scheduled to receive their Social Security payment on Wednesday, September 16. Those born between the 21st and 31st are scheduled for Wednesday, September 23.

Benefits are generally delivered electronically through direct deposit or a Direct Express debit card, meaning recipients don't usually need to take any action for the money to arrive.

A payment may not always appear at exactly the same time for every recipient because individual banks can have different posting procedures.

The SSA advises beneficiaries who do not receive an expected payment to allow three additional mailing days before contacting Social Security.

Anyone expecting money Wednesday should therefore check whether their birthday falls between the 1st and 10th and whether they are covered by one of the exceptions to the standard schedule.

articles.title: Donald Trump, President of the United States, "My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades"
articles.standfirst: Years before returning to the White House, Trump explained why he believed striking back could deter future opponents
articles.summary: Years before returning to the White House, Trump explained why he believed striking back could deter future opponents
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has never made much effort to hide how he responds when he believes he has been wronged.

Years before his political career transformed him from businessman and television personality into president of the United States, Trump laid out that philosophy in Think Big: Make It Happen in Business and Life, the book he wrote with Bill Zanker .

“My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades,” Trump wrote.

It's one of the more striking lines from Trump ’s business writing because it presents retaliation as something more deliberate than anger in the moment.

Trump ’s broader argument was that people are less likely to challenge someone who has established a reputation for responding aggressively when attacked. In his telling, fighting back could protect a person not only from the original adversary but from future ones as well.

Fighting back sends a message

The same theme appears elsewhere in Think Big, where Trump urged readers not to allow opponents to push them around.

“I go after people, and you know what? People do not play around with me as much as they do with others,” Trump wrote in another passage. “They know that if they do, they are in for a big fight.”

His advice wasn't simply to defend oneself. Trump also argued that the response should be memorable enough to influence people watching from the sidelines, presenting retaliation as a form of deterrence.

That philosophy fit naturally with the competitive persona Trump spent decades cultivating in business, which was aim high, push relentlessly and view disputes through the prism of winning and losing.

The words were written as advice about business and life, not as a presidential doctrine. Still, they inevitably attract greater scrutiny now that their author exercises the powers of the presidency.

A different weight from the Oval Office

Trump ’s supporters have frequently praised his instinct to fight back, viewing his unwillingness to absorb attacks quietly as evidence that he will not be intimidated by opponents.

Critics see a potential danger in precisely the same characteristic, particularly when the distinction between political disagreement, institutional conflict and personal grievance becomes important.

It also establishes how Trump chose to describe himself. His message was that retaliation could be useful, that reputation mattered and that allowing an attack to go unanswered risked inviting another one.

Nearly two decades later, the line remains notable because it requires little interpretation. It isn't an assessment from an ally or an accusation from an opponent.

It's Trump , in his own words, explaining how he believed a powerful person should respond when crossed.

articles.title: Alaska Permanent Fund Eligibility: who will be getting their payment for September 2026?
articles.standfirst: Residents waiting for the 2026 dividend should check their status
articles.summary: Residents waiting for the 2026 dividend should check their status
articles.body:
If you’re waiting on an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend in September, the key thing to know is that this month’s payment does not represent the main 2026 PFD distribution.

The Alaska Department of Revenue has scheduled a September 10 payment for people whose 2025 or earlier dividend is still unpaid and whose application was listed as “Eligible-Not Paid” as of September 2.

So if you’re waiting specifically for the 2026 Permanent Fund Dividend , September 10 is generally not your payment date. Most 2026 recipients will need to look ahead to October, when the state begins its main annual distributions.

That distinction matters because being eligible for a 2026 PFD doesn't, by itself, mean you’ll receive money this month. Applicants can check their individual status through the state’s myPFD system to see whether their application is included in the upcoming payment run.

Who qualifies for the 2026 Alaska PFD?

Eligibility for the 2026 dividend is based mainly on your residency and circumstances during calendar year 2025. You must have been an Alaska resident throughout 2025 and, when you applied, intended to remain an Alaska resident indefinitely.

You generally cannot have claimed residency in another state or country, or received a benefit based on such a residency claim, at any point since December 31, 2024.

Time spent outside Alaska can also affect eligibility. If you were absent for more than 180 days, that absence must have fallen under one of the program’s allowable categories.

Applicants must also have been physically present in Alaska for at least 72 consecutive hours at some point during either 2024 or 2025. Certain criminal convictions and periods of incarceration can also make a person ineligible.

That includes being sentenced as a result of a felony conviction during 2025 or being incarcerated during the year because of a felony conviction. Some misdemeanor-related incarceration can also affect eligibility depending on prior convictions.

When will the main 2026 PFD payments arrive?

The first major 2026 PFD payment date is scheduled for October 1.

If you filed online, selected direct deposit and have been determined eligible for payment by September 18, your dividend is scheduled to arrive on that date.

A second major payment is scheduled for October 22. Online and paper applicants determined eligible by October 12 can receive their dividend then, either through direct deposit or by check. Paper checks are also scheduled to begin mailing from Juneau on October 22.

If your eligibility is confirmed after those deadlines, your payment will generally move into one of the following monthly distributions.

So the immediate September date to watch is September 10, but that applies only to older unpaid dividends that met the September 2 eligibility cutoff.

If you’re waiting on the 2026 PFD, the more important dates are in October, along with whatever status appears on your individual application.

articles.title: Girl Scouts’ new cookies are now for ‘man’s best friend,’ without forgetting to innovate in food
articles.standfirst: The 2027 lineup will bring dogs into the Girl Scout tradition while offering families a cookie created without the nine major food allergens
articles.summary: The 2027 lineup will bring dogs into the Girl Scout tradition while offering families a cookie created without the nine major food allergens
articles.body:
For generations, Girl Scout Cookie season has brought families together around colorful boxes, familiar flavors and a tradition that extends far beyond the cookies themselves. But children and parents living with food allergies have not always been able to participate. Meanwhile, the dog waiting hopefully beside the table could only watch. That will change in 2027.

Girl Scouts of the USA is introducing two first-of-their-kind products. Patch Pals will give dogs their own Girl Scout-inspired treat, while Girl Scout Sparkables will become the organization’s first cookie developed for families navigating certain food allergies.

Patch Pals are soft-baked, blueberry muffin-flavored dog treats developed in collaboration with BARK, a company specializing in products for dogs. Each treat will feature one of four “patch” designs representing classic Girl Scout experiences.

The treats were inspired by Girl Scouts’ “deep love for their dogs” and created to celebrate “the bond between people and their pups.” Although Patch Pals are intended for dogs, they are made with human-grade ingredients.

Girl Scout Sparkables open the tradition to more families

The second addition addresses a challenge faced by millions of Americans. Sparkables are crunchy oatmeal cookies with chocolate chips and colorful sprinkles, but what they leave out is just as important as what they contain.

The cookies were created to avoid the nine major food allergens: wheat, tree nuts, peanuts, milk, eggs, soy, fish, sesame and shellfish. They are also gluten-free, nut-free and vegan.

Girl Scouts collaborated on the recipe with Partake, a Black-owned and woman-led company specializing in allergy-friendly foods. Sparkables will be produced in a facility designed to avoid the same nine allergens, giving families dealing with common food allergies a new way to participate in Girl Scout Cookie season.

Approximately 22 million Americans were living with food allergies in 2024, according to the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America . That represents roughly six out of every 100 people in the country.

“Inspired by Girl Scouts around the country who have advocated for expanding the cookie lineup to meet the diverse needs of their communities , Patch Pals and Girl Scout Sparkables offer new ways for more girls, families and beloved pets to participate in the Girl Scout Cookie Program while staying true to what makes the tradition special,” GSUSA said.

Patch Pals and Girl Scout Sparkables will be available exclusively online for direct shipping beginning Jan. 12, 2027, coinciding with the national launch of the 2027 Girl Scout Cookie season. Customers can register for notifications through the organization’s cookie news page or text “COOKIES” to 59618.

Familiar favorites such as Thin Mints, Samoas, Caramel deLites, Tagalongs and Peanut Butter Patties are expected to return. Exploremores, the chocolate, marshmallow and almond-flavored sandwich cookie introduced for the 2026 season, will also remain in the lineup.

Girl Scout Cookie season has always been about more than opening a box. It is about participating in a shared tradition. In 2027, that circle will become a little wider, wide enough for more children, more families and, finally, the dog sitting faithfully beside them.

articles.title: Members of the jury in the Lindsay Clancy case describe exactly what happened: “She’s not guilty...”
articles.standfirst: One juror changed everything in the Lindsay Clancy trial — the panel was ready to clear her.
articles.summary: One juror changed everything in the Lindsay Clancy trial — the panel was ready to clear her.
articles.body:
The foreperson of the jury in the controversial triple murder trial of Lindsay Clancy revealed that the panel came very close to finding her not guilty by reason of insanity , but one juror refused to support that decision, preventing a unanimous verdict.

“He admitted he had reasonable doubt after we watched the video of the interview,” one female juror told NBC 10 Boston in an interview.

Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial last Friday after the jury sent a third note stating that they remained unable to reach a decision.

“There were three forms I had to fill out and I started filling them out, I wrote my signature on each one but then he said, ‘But I’m still not going to say she’s not guilty by reason of insanity.’”

The three women interviewed were identified as Paula , a former government contractor; Kelly , a chef in Plymouth; and Ronnie , the jury foreperson and a retired fifth-grade special education teacher.

The jurors said the member who opposed the verdict was “arrogant” for refusing to engage with the rest of the panel and for not considering their arguments regarding the evidence presented during the trial.

“He was very arrogant. He really did not take anything that anybody said,” one of the women claimed.

Another juror explained that, during the lengthy deliberations, members of the panel walked around the room out of frustration.

“Every one of us in the hours of our frustration would get up and walk the room because you just couldn’t sit anymore. And we would all go to the cart with the exhibits. He, I think, got up to the cart once very briefly and went back to his seat.”

“He would not interact with us and try to understand,” she continued. “We read to him, on numerous occasions, the definition of reasonable doubt from Judge [William] Sullivan’s instruction.”

“But he had the hardest time getting over the fact that Lindsay viciously killed her children,” she explained.

The women also felt that prosecutors did not show enough compassion toward Clancy, who was described during the trial as a mother suffering from severe insomnia, anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, and thoughts of harming her childre n in the months leading up to the killings.

“I just found it to be harsh — very, very harsh,” one juror said.

“The fact that they had no character witnesses in regards to Lindsay being a bad mother … I found it to be biased.”

The foreperson said all the witnesses and evidence “proved that she loved her children … so she had to have snapped.”

The jury, made up of nine women and three men , deliberated for approximately 38 hours over seven days before reaching an impasse. The members informed the judge they could not reach an agreement on Tuesday, repeated that warning on Wednesday, and finally did so again on Friday, when Sullivan declared a mistrial.

Clancy’s defense team asked the jury to find her not criminally responsible, arguing that she suffered from severe postpartum psychosis and heard a voice commanding her to strangle her three children: Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months, on Jan. 24, 2023.

Prosecutors, however, argued that Clancy carefully planned the killings and fabricated the story about hearing a voice and experiencing a psychotic episode in order to avoid criminal responsibility.

The case sparked a major debate in the United States over maternal mental health, postpartum psychosis, and the medical care provided to new mothers.

During the trial, Reddington argued that Clancy received inadequate care from a psychiatrist and other specialists, who allegedly failed to properly diagnose her condition and prescribed her 13 powerful psychiatric medications in the four months leading up to the killings.

articles.title: Donald Trump, President of the United States: "My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades"
articles.standfirst: A line from Donald Trump’s 2007 book Think Big captures the combative philosophy that has followed him from New York real estate and television into his political career and the White House
articles.summary: A line from Donald Trump’s 2007 book Think Big captures the combative philosophy that has followed him from New York real estate and television into his political career and the White House
articles.body:
D onald Trump has spent decades cultivating an image built around confidence, confrontation and the determination to avoid being seen as the weaker side in a dispute.

Long before he became president, Trump repeatedly presented retaliation as an important part of his approach to business and personal conflicts.

One of the clearest examples appeared in his 2007 book Think Big: Make It Happen in Business and Life, where he wrote: “My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades.”

The quote has continued to attract attention because it neatly reflects a recurring theme in Trump's public persona: the idea that responding forcefully to an opponent can serve as both a warning and a way of maintaining leverage.

The philosophy did not begin with his political career. Trump built his public identity as a New York businessman, later expanding into television, publishing and eventually presidential politics.

He took over his father's real estate company in the early 1970s and became associated with high-profile developments, before publishing The Art of the Deal in 1987.

That book helped establish many of the themes that would later become synonymous with Trump's brand.

He portrayed deal-making as an aggressive contest in which confidence, publicity and the willingness to push hard could provide an advantage. His later books expanded on that worldview.

Trump's philosophy of fighting back

In Think Big, the statement about getting even appeared alongside other advice emphasizing the importance of responding when somebody attempts to take advantage of you.

Another passage attributed to Trump advises: “When someone crosses you, my advice is ‘Get even!’” He went on to argue that people who attack or wrong you should be confronted rather than simply ignored.

The language is striking because it goes beyond conventional business advice about negotiation. Trump presented retaliation as a way of establishing boundaries and discouraging future attacks.

That attitude became an important part of his political identity after he entered presidential politics.

Trump's political career has repeatedly been marked by public clashes with opponents, journalists, political rivals and institutions.

His supporters have often interpreted this willingness to fight as evidence that he is unwilling to back down, while critics have argued that his confrontational style can deepen political divisions.

His first presidential campaign in 2016 transformed that approach into a national political strategy.

After winning the presidency, Trump continued to communicate directly with the public through social media and other channels, frequently responding to criticism with personal attacks or challenges of his own.

The combative style has remained part of his second presidency.

The White House identifies Trump as both the 45th and 47th president of the United States, following his return to office after winning the 2024 election.

His administration describes his political career as an extension of his earlier business success and emphasizes his willingness to challenge established political conventions.

Trump's supporters have long viewed that approach as part of his appeal. Rather than presenting himself as a traditional politician, he has often described politics in competitive terms, with opponents cast as people who must be defeated rather than simply disagreed with.

That makes the old Think Big quotation particularly revealing when viewed alongside his later career.

The statement, however, should be understood in its original context. It was written years before Trump entered the White House and formed part of a broader collection of advice about business, competition and dealing with adversaries. It was not written as a statement of presidential policy.

Trump's writing career has been extensive. The White House describes him as the author of more than 14 books, with The Art of the Deal among his best-known works.

His publishing career also included titles such as The Art of the Comeback, How to Get Rich, Think Big and Think Like a Champion.

The distinction matters because Trump's business philosophy and presidential responsibilities operate in very different environments.

A real-estate negotiation can be framed as a contest between parties trying to secure the best possible outcome. Presidential decisions, by contrast, involve constitutional responsibilities, foreign relations, economic policy and the interests of millions of Americans.

Nevertheless, Trump's personal style has remained remarkably consistent across those different stages of his career.

The line “My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades” is therefore more than an isolated quotation from one of his books. It forms part of a broader body of writing in which Trump repeatedly described confrontation, toughness and the refusal to accept perceived mistreatment as essential elements of his approach.

Nearly two decades after Think Big was published, that philosophy remains closely associated with the public image Trump has built, first as a businessman and television personality, and ultimately as a two-time elected president of the United States.

articles.title: Engineers don't know how this 1933 Cleveland bridge is still standing despite a catastrophic flaw
articles.standfirst: This infrastructure will remain closed until further notice from the authorities
articles.summary: This infrastructure will remain closed until further notice from the authorities
articles.body:
With nearly 100 years of history , experts still wonder how it is possible that the Brookpark Road bridge has remained intact. In a new analysis, very significant deterioration has been detected, which has led the authorities to decree the immediate closure of the crossing until further notice. Now, engineers are working on possible medium-term solutions.

It should be borne in mind that this road is used by many pedestrians and vehicles every day. It is part of State Route 17 and is near Cleveland Hopkins International Airport . Among the reasons given by the Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT), they note that it has been closed for “precaution” and to preserve “public safety”.

Brookpark Road bridge will remain closed until it is “safe” for travelers

The truth is that the bridge rehabilitation work was scheduled for 2028. However, the analyses carried out in recent months have revealed the possibility of it collapsing. They have realized that the deterioration of the beams that support the roadways is more advanced than might have been expected.

Brent Kovacs, spokesperson for Ohio Department of Transportation District 12, has provided the reasons that led the authorities to make this decision on Fox 8. “We always say that if a road or a bridge is not safe for motorists, we close it immediately , and that is truly the case,” emphasizes one of those responsible for infrastructure safety.

“We believe this is the safest measure we can take, rather than reducing the load, reducing the lanes, or doing something temporary” , Kovacs concluded. Thus, now all that remains is to analyze which alternatives are available and determine which is the best solution so that the timelines are as short as possible.

articles.title: 2027 Social Security Benefits Changes: Increases, cuts, and bills that could change your benefits next year
articles.standfirst: Retirees are likely to see another raise next year, but some of the biggest benefit concerns are further down the road
articles.summary: Retirees are likely to see another raise next year, but some of the biggest benefit concerns are further down the road
articles.body:
Social Security recipients are heading toward another increase in 2027, but the bigger story is becoming more complicated than a simple COLA boost.

Current forecasts suggest beneficiaries could receive a cost-of-living adjustment of roughly 3.5% to 3.6% next year, potentially giving retirees a larger monthly increase than they received in 2026.

The Senior Citizens League ’s latest estimate stands at 3.6%, while AARP has projected about 3.5%. Neither figure is official.

That number won't be finalized until October 14, when the government releases the final inflation data used in the calculation.

A 3.6% COLA would add roughly $72 per month to a $2,000 Social Security benefit. Someone receiving $2,500 per month would see an increase of about $90 before deductions such as Medicare premiums.

The 2027 COLA still only a forecast

Social Security ’s annual adjustment is based on the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, known as the CPI-W.

The government compares the average CPI-W for July, August and September 2026 with the corresponding third-quarter average used for the previous COLA.

The percentage increase, rounded to the nearest one-tenth of 1%, becomes the official 2027 adjustment. That means forecasts can still move before October.

Other annual Social Security figures are also likely to change, including the maximum amount of earnings subject to payroll taxes and earnings limits for some beneficiaries who continue working before reaching full retirement age.

No broad Social Security benefit cut approved

One source of confusion has been discussion around proposals that could reduce future cost-of-living adjustments or change how inflation is measured. Those proposals aren't current policy.

The Social Security Administration publishes actuarial analyses showing what would happen if Congress adopted different reforms. Some involve lower COLAs, while others would increase benefits for certain groups or change taxation.

None of those models amount to an approved across-the-board cut for 2027. Full retirement age also is not scheduled to rise again under current law.

The age has reached 67 for people affected by the final stage of the previously legislated increase.

“Under current law, it does not go any higher,” certified public accountant Geoffrey Schmidt told Yahoo Finance. “So if you’ve been worried they’ll keep moving the goalposts on you, at least on the retirement age, that increase is over.”

The real threat comes later

The more serious concern is Social Security ’s long-term funding outlook. The latest trustees’ projections indicate that the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund could be depleted in the early 2030s if Congress doesn't act.

That doesn't mean Social Security would disappear. Payroll tax revenue would continue flowing into the system, allowing the government to pay a substantial portion of scheduled benefits even after reserves are exhausted.

Still, that projected shortfall is why lawmakers continue debating changes involving taxes, benefits and COLA formulas. Those discussions matter greatly for the future, but they should not be confused with an imminent 2027 cut.

Right now, the key date is October 14. That is when beneficiaries will finally learn the official COLA and have a clearer picture of how much their monthly checks could rise in January.

articles.title: Costco upcoming warehouse locations: Where and when are the new stores being opened?
articles.standfirst: Costco’s latest expansion includes new warehouses, a business center and several openings with dates already confirmed
articles.summary: Costco’s latest expansion includes new warehouses, a business center and several openings with dates already confirmed
articles.body:
Costco is preparing another major round of expansion, with 14 new warehouses scheduled to open across the United States and Canada as the retailer continues adding locations at a rapid pace.

The upcoming openings stretch from California and Texas to New York, Virginia and several Canadian markets, giving Costco a broader footprint without entering any entirely new U.S. states.

Some locations already have specific opening dates, while others are still listed only by month. Together, they represent the next stage of a much larger growth plan that could see Costco continue opening dozens of warehouses every year.

The company has already expanded in several U.S. states in 2026, as well as internationally, and chief executive Ron Vachris has said Costco wants to open 30 or more warehouses annually over the next five to 10 years.

Where Costco’s next warehouses are opening

The confirmed upcoming U.S. locations are:

- Chandler, Arizona Business Center

Costco also has four Canadian openings planned:

- Northeast Edmonton, Alberta

Several of the U.S. sites already have more detailed schedules. Lee’s Summit is expected to open October 2, Amherst is targeting October 28 and Camarillo is scheduled for October 30. Other locations haven't yet been given specific public opening dates.

The Chandler project will be a Costco Business Center , which differs slightly from a traditional warehouse by placing more emphasis on products for restaurants, offices and commercial customers. Regular Costco members can still shop there.

Not every opening represents a new market

Some of the projects are expansions or replacements rather than Costco arriving in a community for the first time.

The Newport News warehouse, for example, is expected to replace an existing Costco that has served the Virginia city since 1988. The company purchased a larger nearby site for a new warehouse and fuel station.

Other projects already have pieces of their operations running. The gas station connected to the Camarillo location opened ahead of the warehouse, while Amherst has also begun fuel operations before its full store opening.

Costco ’s continued growth follows a broader strategy of expanding both domestically and internationally.

Vachris has indicated that roughly half of the company’s planned annual openings could be in the United States, with additional expansion expected in Canada, Mexico, Asia, Europe, Australia and New Zealand.

More U.S. projects are also in development or under consideration in places such as Downey and Fresno in California, Charleston County in South Carolina, Hillsborough County in Florida, Southborough in Massachusetts, Silver Spring in Maryland, Scottsdale in Arizona and Des Plaines in Illinois.

articles.title: Charlie Kirk, activist, "Never give up. Never surrender. Always go for the win"
articles.standfirst: His message from The MAGA Doctrine centered on refusing defeat and continuing to pursue the result you want
articles.summary: His message from The MAGA Doctrine centered on refusing defeat and continuing to pursue the result you want
articles.body:
Success rarely follows a straight line, and Charlie Kirk once offered a particularly uncomplicated answer for what to do when things start going wrong.. keep going.

“Never give up. Never surrender. Always go for the win.” The line, attributed to Kirk in his book The MAGA Doctrine: The Only Ideas That Will Win the Future , is brief enough to sound almost like a locker-room instruction.

Yet it captures a broader philosophy about ambition, resilience and what happens after an individual encounters resistance.

Kirk didn't frame the message around accepting defeat gracefully or lowering expectations after a setback. His language was deliberately competitive. Continuing wasn't enough on its own as the ultimate objective remained winning.

Persistence ahead of immediate results

There's an important difference between losing and giving up, and Kirk ’s statement rests almost entirely on that separation. Failure can describe an outcome at a particular moment. Surrender is a decision to stop pursuing the goal altogether.

“Never give up. Never surrender,” Kirk wrote before adding the final instruction: “Always go for the win.”

That last part transforms the passage from a straightforward call for resilience into something more ambitious. Kirk wasn't simply encouraging people to endure difficulties.

He was arguing that they should continue pursuing the result they originally wanted, even after circumstances become difficult. The idea can be applied far beyond the political setting of The MAGA Doctrine .

Careers stall, businesses fail, athletes lose, students fall short and personal plans sometimes collapse despite considerable effort.

Kirk ’s answer wasn't to pretend those setbacks didn't matter. It was to refuse to allow them to determine what happened next.

Why the message remains easy to understand

Motivational advice can quickly become complicated, particularly when it attempts to provide a formula for success. Kirk ’s statement does the opposite.

It offers no guarantee that persistence will ultimately produce victory, nor does it explain when a person should reconsider a particular strategy. Its appeal comes instead from the clarity of the attitude it promotes.

Someone can lose and try again. Someone can be disappointed without becoming defeated. An objective can become harder without automatically becoming impossible.

That is what makes “Never give up. Never surrender. Always go for the win” an easily transferable piece of advice.

The quote originated in a political book and came from an activist whose views generated strong support as well as intense opposition.

People don't have to share Kirk ’s political beliefs, however, to recognize the broader principle contained in those words. Setbacks are inevitable. Surrender is optional.

The Powerball jackpot has climbed past the $200 million mark after another drawing ended without a grand-prize winner, leaving players with a fresh shot at a major payout on Wednesday, September 9.

The estimated jackpot now stands at $207 million , with a cash option of $89.3 million for a winner who chooses the lump-sum payment instead of the annuity.

Wednesday’s drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. ET . The winning numbers haven't yet been drawn and will be confirmed after the official results are released.

Powerball winning numbers for Wednesday, September 9, 2026

Players should keep their tickets until the official drawing results have been verified.

Why the Powerball jackpot has grown to $207 million

The prize increased after Monday’s drawing failed to produce a jackpot winner.

The winning numbers for September 7 were 15, 19, 28, 39 and 56, with a Powerball of 3. The Power Play multiplier was 3x.

Nobody matched all six numbers to claim the jackpot. There were also no tickets matching all five white balls for the $1 million Match 5 prize, while no player secured the $2 million Match 5 plus Power Play payout.

That allowed the jackpot to roll over to Wednesday. Powerball drawings are held three times each week, on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday nights.

A standard ticket costs $2. Players select five numbers from 1 to 69 before choosing a separate Powerball number from 1 to 26.

The jackpot requires matching all five white balls and the red Powerball , but smaller prizes are available for several other combinations. Matching only the Powerball is enough to win $4.

What would a $207 million Powerball winner actually receive?

The advertised Powerball jackpot reflects the estimated value of the annuity option.

A winner selecting the annuity would receive an initial payment followed by 29 annual payments that increase over time.

Someone choosing the cash option would instead receive approximately $89.3 million before taxes.

Players can add Power Play for an additional $1, allowing most non-jackpot prizes to be multiplied depending on the number selected during the drawing.

Double Play is also available in participating jurisdictions for another $1 and provides a separate chance to win a top prize of $10 million.

The latest jackpot run comes less than a month after one of the biggest Powerball prizes of 2026 was claimed.

An Illinois ticket won a $1.04 billion jackpot on August 12, resetting the game before the current prize began building again.

Wednesday night will decide whether the $207 million jackpot finds a winner or continues growing toward Saturday’s drawing.

articles.title: Trump promises a $5,000 check to every adult if Republicans win the November elections and sets only one condition
articles.standfirst: This would be his controversial ‘dividend’ that would cost him one trillion euros
articles.summary: This would be his controversial ‘dividend’ that would cost him one trillion euros
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump has promised to deliver $5,000 (about €4,300) to every adult American citizen if the Republican Party manages to retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November midterm elections . The announcement was made this Wednesday during the Republican National Convention held in Dallas, at a time when Republicans are facing elections in which control of Congress is at stake.

Trump presented the measure as a “ dividend ” for citizens and assured that it would be linked to the economic strength of the United States. “If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both, due to our tremendous strength and economic success, I will issue a $5,000 dividend to every adult citizen of the United States ,” he stated during his speech.

The president added one condition: the money would have to be spent within the United States . He did not explain, however, how the payments would be made, when they would begin to be received, which agency would be responsible for distributing them, or what exactly the source of funding would be. Nor did he specify during his speech whether all adult citizens would be entitled to the money regardless of their income.

A promise of more than one trillion dollars

The economic dimension of the proposal is one of the main questions. The United States has approximately 270 million adults, so giving $5,000 to each one would entail an outlay of around $1.35 trillion , according to estimates reported by Reuters.

The figure is considerably higher than the direct payment programs approved during the coronavirus pandemic , when the U.S. Congress authorized several rounds of aid for households. On this occasion, moreover, Trump did not present a specific legislative program, but rather made the announcement during a political event. CBS notes that he also did not clarify whether he intends to ask Congress to authorize the payments.

Funding is another of the unresolved issues. Trump did not explain where the money would come from in his speech. Some subsequent reports point to the revenue obtained through trade tariffs as a possible source, although current revenue from this route would not be sufficient on its own to cover an amount of this size.

The proposal also raises questions about its implementation. To carry out a payment program of this magnitude, it would be necessary to determine its legal basis and the corresponding budgetary mechanism. Associated Press notes that the measure would likely need approval from Congress and that there is still no approved program guaranteeing those $5,000.

articles.title: Social Security Max Contribution 2026: How much do you have to add to get $3,000 a month in Social Security?
articles.standfirst: A $3,000 monthly Social Security check is within reach for some workers, but your earnings history and claiming age matter far more than simply how much you pay in
articles.summary: A $3,000 monthly Social Security check is within reach for some workers, but your earnings history and claiming age matter far more than simply how much you pay in
articles.body:
For Americans planning for retirement, Social Security can become one of the most important pieces of the income puzzle.

But reaching a target such as $3,000 per month requires more than simply paying a certain amount into the program.

The Social Security Administration calculates retirement benefits using a worker's earnings history, including the highest 35 years of indexed earnings.

The age at which someone claims benefits also has a major impact on the final monthly check.

In 2026, the Social Security taxable maximum is $184,500. That means workers generally pay Social Security payroll taxes only on the first $184,500 they earn during the year.

The employee tax rate is 6.2%, meaning someone who reaches the taxable maximum would have $11,439 withheld for Social Security during 2026. Employers pay a matching 6.2%, bringing the combined Social Security tax rate to 12.4%.

However, that $11,439 figure should not be confused with a required "contribution" for receiving $3,000 per month.

There is no single amount that a worker can contribute in 2026 to guarantee a $3,000 monthly retirement benefit. Social Security is based on a person's lifetime earnings record rather than a retirement-account balance.

The distinction is important because earning $184,500 in one year does not automatically put someone on track for a $3,000 monthly check. The worker would generally need a substantial earnings history over many years.

How much do you need to earn for a $3,000 Social Security check?

The SSA's benefit formula starts with a worker's average indexed monthly earnings, or AIME. For someone becoming eligible in 2026, the formula applies 90% to the first $1,286 of AIME, 32% to the portion between $1,286 and $7,749, and 15% to earnings above $7,749.

That progressive formula means workers don't need to earn the maximum taxable amount throughout their careers to receive a substantial Social Security benefit.

A worker who reaches an AIME of roughly $7,044 could produce a primary insurance amount around $3,000 under the 2026 formula, before any adjustment for claiming early or delayed retirement.

The actual calculation is more complicated because the SSA wage-indexes previous earnings and selects the highest 35 years.

For comparison, the SSA says the maximum retirement benefit for someone retiring at full retirement age in 2026 is $4,152 per month. A person claiming at 62 in 2026 could receive a maximum of $2,969, while someone who waits until 70 could receive as much as $5,181.

That illustrates why the age at which benefits begin matters so much.

For people reaching age 62 in 2026, full retirement age is 67. Claiming before that point reduces the monthly benefit, while delaying after full retirement age can increase the payment through delayed retirement credits.

The 35-year requirement also matters. If a worker has fewer than 35 years of covered earnings, the SSA includes zeros for the missing years, which can substantially reduce the average used to calculate benefits.

Likewise, earning more than the Social Security taxable maximum in a particular year does not create an unlimited benefit. Once earnings reach $184,500 in 2026, additional wages do not increase the amount of income subject to the 6.2% Social Security tax.

For self-employed workers, the calculation looks different because they generally pay both the employee and employer portions of Social Security and Medicare taxes.

The combined Social Security rate is 12.4%, subject to the annual taxable maximum. The IRS confirms that the 2026 wage base is $184,500.

Ultimately, there is no magic contribution that unlocks a $3,000 monthly Social Security check. The most reliable way to determine whether you're on track is to review your earnings record and benefit estimate through your my Social Security account.

The key factors are straightforward: build a strong 35-year earnings record, understand the annual taxable maximum and carefully consider when to claim benefits.

For some workers, $3,000 a month is achievable. But it is the result of decades of covered earnings and a strategic claiming decision, not simply reaching a particular contribution amount in 2026.

articles.title: Are banks open on September 11? Mail delivery, banks and everything that will be open this Patriot Day
articles.standfirst: September 11, 2026, marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks
articles.summary: September 11, 2026, marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks
articles.body:
A mericans will pause on Friday, September 11, to remember the nearly 3,000 people killed in the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001.

The date is officially recognized as Patriot Day and the National Day of Service and Remembrance, but that designation does not make September 11 a federal holiday.

That distinction is important for anyone wondering whether everyday services will be available.

The Office of Personnel Management's official 2026 federal holiday calendar does not include September 11. The next federal holiday after Labor Day is Columbus Day on October 12.

As a result, Friday will generally function like a normal business day across the United States.

Are banks open on September 11?

Yes. Most banks are expected to be open on Friday, September 11, 2026, because Patriot Day is not included among the federal holidays observed by the banking system.

Customers should therefore be able to visit bank branches during their normal Friday hours, although individual branches can have different opening and closing times. Online banking, mobile banking and ATMs should also remain available.

The distinction between Patriot Day and an actual federal holiday is significant. Federal holidays include dates such as New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas . September 11 is not on that list.

People who need to deposit checks, withdraw cash, visit a teller or handle other in-person banking business should not generally expect a nationwide closure.

Will the mail be delivered on September 11?

Yes. Regular USPS mail delivery is expected to continue on September 11.

Post offices are also expected to maintain their normal Friday schedules because the U.S. Postal Service's holiday-related closures generally correspond with recognized federal holidays.

Since September 11 is not a federal holiday, there is no nationwide USPS shutdown planned for Patriot Day.

That means customers should expect regular residential mail delivery and normal post-office operations, although individual locations can have their own schedules.

For most Americans, September 11 will not result in widespread closures.

Government offices are generally expected to operate normally, as are schools and most businesses. Grocery stores, restaurants, retailers, gas stations and other everyday services should also follow their regular Friday schedules.

The stock market is likewise not scheduled to close for Patriot Day . The major U.S. financial markets observe a specific holiday calendar, and September 11 is not among the scheduled market holidays.

However, individual companies, schools, municipalities or organizations can choose to hold memorial events or modify their schedules.

The day remains an important national observance even without being a federal holiday. Patriot Day was established to honor those who died in the September 11 attacks and to remember the victims of the attack on the World Trade Center, the Pentagon and the passengers and crew of United Airlines Flight 93.

The 25th anniversary in 2026 is expected to bring particularly significant commemorations across the country, with ceremonies, moments of silence and memorial events planned in communities nationwide.

Presidentially issued proclamations also call for the American flag to be displayed at half-staff on September 11, while Americans are encouraged to observe a moment of silence in remembrance.

So, while banks, post offices and most businesses will be open on Friday, September 11, 2026, the day carries a very different significance from an ordinary Friday. Americans will be able to go about their normal routines while also marking one of the most consequential days in modern U.S. history.

articles.title: September 11, 25 years later: the attack that changed the world and whose consequences still endure
articles.standfirst: A quarter century has passed since the attacks that claimed the lives of 2,977 people and triggered a global war on terror that transformed world geopolitics
articles.summary: A quarter century has passed since the attacks that claimed the lives of 2,977 people and triggered a global war on terror that transformed world geopolitics
articles.body:
On September 11, 2001, the world stood still for a few minutes. At 8:48 a.m. local time in New York, a commercial airplane crashed into the North Tower of the World Trade Center. Fifteen minutes later, a second plane struck the South Tower. What initially seemed like an accident became, before the television cameras, one of the most traumatic episodes in recent history.

A quarter of a century later, the images of the Twin Towers collapsing remain part of the collective memory, but the consequences of that day go far beyond New York. 9/11 triggered a profound transformation in international politics, security, relations between the West and the Middle East, and the very nature of the terrorist threat.

The official death toll rose to 2,977 people. Of those, 2,753 died at the World Trade Center and another 224 were killed when two other planes crashed into the Pentagon and in Pennsylvania.

In Spain, the first impact occurred when there were barely 12 minutes left until 3:00 p.m. While a sunny morning was beginning in New York, within a few minutes the Manhattan sky was covered by a gigantic cloud of dust and smoke.

But the attacks did not end at the Twin Towers. A third plane crashed into the Pentagon and a fourth aircraft went down in a field in Shanksville, in Pennsylvania, after the passengers rebelled against the hijackers. It is believed that the target was another symbol of American power, although it never reached it.

George W. Bush's response: a war without borders

U.S. President George W. Bush interpreted the attacks as a declaration of war. In his memoir, "Decision Points," he compared what happened to Pearl Harbor and assumed that he had to lead a new phase aimed at protecting the United States.

The response came quickly. On October 7, 2001, less than a month after the attacks, the United States began bombing Afghanistan, where the Taliban regime was sheltering Al Qaeda and Osama Bin Laden, identified as the main person responsible for the attacks.

The intervention initially succeeded in expelling Al Qaeda from the country, but it did not put an end to the conflict. Two decades of war, thousands of victims, and enormous destruction left Afghanistan plunged into a situation of extreme fragility. In August 2021, the Taliban recaptured Kabul, symbolically closing a circle that had begun after 9/11.

The second major consequence of that policy came approximately a year and a half later with Iraq. The United States led an invasion in 2003 to overthrow Saddam Hussein arguing that the regime possessed weapons of mass destruction. Those weapons were never found, and the evidence used to justify the military intervention turned out to be false.

The fall of Saddam Hussein gave way to years of violence, instability, and terrorism. The U.S. withdrawal in 2011 left a scenario in which Al Qaeda was able to reorganize, and from which the self-proclaimed Islamic State (ISIS) would later emerge.

The human and economic consequences of that war on terror were enormous. According to the study Costs of War, produced by the Watson Institute for International and Public Affairs at Brown University, the United States' wars in Afghanistan, Iraq and Pakistan have incurred an approximate cost of four trillion dollars.

The death toll in those three conflicts is estimated at between 272,000 and 329,000 deaths, although the figures are subject to different estimates and do not include all the indirect consequences resulting from decades of violence.

The legacy of 9/11 also cannot be understood solely through the wars. The attacks ushered in a new era of security checks, surveillance, and counterterrorism. In airports, at borders, and in intelligence services, the post-9/11 world came to be marked by a постоянная concern about the terrorist threat.

From Al Qaeda to the Islamic State

The invasion of Iraq also had a consequence that would end up shaping international security during the following years. The destabilization of the country favored the emergence and expansion of new jihadist groups.

Al Qaeda maintained significant operational capacity for years, but began to lose prominence after the death of Osama Bin Laden in 2011 and the advance of counterterrorism operations. At the same time, ISIS gained ground until it became a global threat, especially from 2014 onward, when it broke away from Al Qaeda and expanded its activities.

Their strategy also incorporated a new dimension: the recruitment and radicalization of individuals in Western countries. The so-called "lone wolves" carried out attacks using vehicles, knives, and other rudimentary means, making it more difficult to prevent attacks that did not necessarily require large terrorist structures.

A quarter of a century later

25 years later, 9/11 continues to be much more than the date of an attack. It was the starting point of a new geopolitical era whose effects are still felt in much of the world.

The Twin Towers are no longer part of New York's skyline, but their absence remains one of the most powerful symbols of the 21st century. Afghanistan and Iraq continue to bear the consequences of those interventions, jihadist terrorism has evolved, and international politics continues to be shaped by the decisions made in the months and years following that September 11.

The world that woke up that morning in 2001 no longer exists. And a quarter of a century later, the wounds opened that day have still not fully healed.

articles.title: Philadelphia installed white roofs on seniors' homes: temperatures dropped and electricity consumption decreased by 560 kWh per year
articles.standfirst: The initiative managed to reduce roof temperatures by between 4 and 5 degrees Fahrenheit
articles.summary: The initiative managed to reduce roof temperatures by between 4 and 5 degrees Fahrenheit
articles.body:
A solution as simple as painting roofs white . That was the basis of an initiative that demonstrated more than two decades ago that advanced technologies are not always necessary to combat high temperatures . Between 2001 and 2003, the Philadelphia Energy Coordinating Agency (ECA) carried out a pilot project that made it possible to improve the thermal conditions of about 340 homes occupied by low-income older adults.

The selected buildings were located mainly in the northern and western neighborhoods of Philadelphia, where the so-called ‘row houses’, the city’s characteristic terraced homes, received a very basic treatment: the roofs were painted white .

Less heat and lower energy consumption

The project's results were especially striking as well as functional. Measurements taken afterward showed that the temperature of the roofs decreased by approximately between 4 and 5 degrees Fahrenheit, which is equivalent to between 2.2 and 2.8 degrees Celsius .

The improvement was especially significant in the bedrooms located on the upper floors that did not have air conditioning. By receiving less direct solar radiation, the white roofs absorbed less heat and helped prevent temperatures inside the rooms from rising.

The effect also carried over to energy consumption . According to the data provided by the project, the homes whose roofs were painted recorded an approximate reduction of 560 kilowatt-hours per year in the electricity used for air conditioning.

The Philadelphia experience is striking for the simplicity of the intervention. No solar panels, smart climate control systems, or sophisticated technological devices were installed. The action consisted solely of applying white paint to the roofs .

The project exposed the potential of reflective roofs as a simple and effective tool to reduce the impact of solar radiation and heat, especially in vulnerable homes and in urban areas where high temperatures can become a problem during the warmest months.

articles.title: The consequences of 9/11, this is the fee you pay on an airline ticket since the attacks on the Twin Towers
articles.standfirst: Money that is allocated to air transport security
articles.summary: Money that is allocated to air transport security
articles.body:
Just a few minutes before 3:00 p.m. in Spain, 25 years ago, the world changed. The terrorist attacks of 9/11 brought about a total change in people's lives. One of the most important was air travel. The hijacking of the planes that crashed into the Twin Towers and the Pentagon marked the starting point of a new reality in the ways of traveling; from that moment on, the rules for boarding planes changed, and that is something we have all noticed.

From the weeks following the attacks, the security of countries, that of airports and of the airlines themselves underwent a drastic change in the name of security and with the aim of preventing situations like those that occurred that morning of September 11, 2001, from happening again.

The first to take measures were the Americans who, through the Transportation Security Administration (TSA, its acronym in English) , implemented a ‘security fee to help fund the increased cost of security in the country’s air transportation’, which is how it is described on the website of the United States Department of Homeland Security.

Fee applied to flights originating in the United States

In this way, and as has been reported on the website for 25 years, the cost of plane tickets on routes originating in the land of the stars and stripes has a security fee called 'TSA' added to the ticket price.

Its amount is $5.60, a little less than 5 euros, money that is collected and goes directly into the coffers of the U.S. Treasury and is used to pay for part of the security measures implemented over the last 25 years. It is no small amount, since in the accumulated total for all flights in 2025, revenue reached nearly $4 billion . Money that is used to pay the salaries of officers who screen passengers and baggage, so-called Air Marshals, and to invest in new security systems such as scanners and security arches.

articles.title: The story of United Flight 23, the suspected fifth 9/11 plane that was grounded just in time
articles.standfirst: The aircraft never left JFK, but crew members say what happened around the flight has troubled them ever since
articles.summary: The aircraft never left JFK, but crew members say what happened around the flight has troubled them ever since
articles.body:
Among the countless stories that emerged from September 11 , one has remained unusually difficult to resolve: whether a fifth commercial jet was ever meant to join the four planes hijacked that morning.

United Airlines Flight 23 was scheduled to leave New York’s JFK Airport for Los Angeles at about 9 a.m. It had already pushed back and begun taxiing when the attacks forced authorities to shut down air traffic and send planes back to their gates.

The flight never took off. What happened before and after that decision has led several crew members to believe something far more serious may have been unfolding aboard the aircraft.

Former first officer Carol Timmons later described how the cockpit was secured as the plane returned to the terminal.

Flight attendants had reportedly become concerned about a group of passengers whose behavior stood out, including several men who appeared agitated when the departure was canceled.

“The FBI asks questions,” Timmons later said. “They don’t tell you things.”

Flight drew immediate FBI attention

Timmons and other members of the Flight 23 crew were reportedly questioned by federal investigators after the attacks.

Accounts surrounding the flight have also included claims that investigators showed crew members photographs or lineups as they tried to determine whether any of the passengers were connected to the broader 9/11 plot.

TMZ documentary 9/11: The Fifth Plane later collected testimony from pilots, flight attendants, an airline dispatcher and others who said they remained convinced Flight 23 deserved closer scrutiny.

The documentary also presented allegations that suspicious individuals may have entered or returned to the aircraft after it had been evacuated.

Other reports have claimed that box cutters and material linked to Al Qaeda were found in luggage associated with passengers from the flight.

Those claims have never been publicly confirmed in the same way as the evidence surrounding the four hijacked aircraft.

No official conclusion settled mystery

The 9/11 Commission didn't identify Flight 23 as a confirmed fifth hijacking attempt, and there has never been a publicly established finding that terrorists had definitively selected the aircraft for an attack.

That gap between witness accounts and official confirmation is why the story continues to attract attention.

Timmons and others have said the events of that morning left them convinced the shutdown of U.S. airspace may have prevented something catastrophic.

Their belief is significant, but it is still important to separate that belief from what has been formally proven. The crew was questioned. Suspicious behavior was reported. Law enforcement showed interest in the flight.

What remains unconfirmed is that Flight 23 was supposed to become the fifth hijacked plane of September 11. More than two decades later, that uncertainty is exactly what keeps the story alive.

articles.title: Fraud or genius? The truth behind Trump’s $5,000 midterm cheque and what it will actually cost you in taxes
articles.standfirst: The president promises $5,000 to each adult if Republicans win in November
articles.summary: The president promises $5,000 to each adult if Republicans win in November
articles.body:
The latest electoral maneuver by the President of the United States, Donald Trump , has triggered an avalanche of reactions. The leader has promised $5,000 to every adult American if the Republicans win the November elections . Spanish economist Santiago Niño Becerra , through a message posted on social media, has expressed great surprise at this initiative.

The Spanish professor began his presentation by analyzing the economic outlay that keeping his word would entail: " One trillion dollars . That is the amount that President Trump's promise to give 5,000 dollars to every adult will reach if the Republican Party wins the November elections. Impossible? Not at all ".

Beyond making it clear that it is feasible numerically, Santiago Niño Becerra has reflected on the ethics of the measure proposed by President Donald Trump . "Leaving aside the legality of such a promise, doesn't it sound like vote-buying?" , he asked.

Donald Trump's formula for fulfilling his promise

In addition, the expert has put forward the formula that the Republican leader could use to deal with this surprising election promise. "To pay that amount, the United States only has to issue 1 trillion dollars more in debt . After all, if it now has 40, it will have 41. Food for thought," the economist explained in his social media post.

This is the "Trump Dividend"

"If the Republicans win, you win with us and receive $5,000. It will be called the Trump Dividend ." This is how the president expressed his electoral initiative, a move that, despite being surprising, is not entirely new for the leader of the United States . Last year, as AP has recalled, D onald Trump gave members of the armed forces a check for $1,776 . It was called the "Warrior Dividend" . The White House has not offered many details about its proposal, but Vice President JD Vance clarified that this "Trump Dividend" would not go to the richest.

articles.title: Rudy Giuliani, former NYC Mayor, "The lesson of 9/11 is that America is truly exceptional"
articles.standfirst: The former mayor says the attacks were meant to divide America but instead brought the country closer together
articles.summary: The former mayor says the attacks were meant to divide America but instead brought the country closer together
articles.body:
Rudy Giuliani ’s most enduring reflections on September 11 have focused less on the destruction itself than on what happened afterward.

The former New York City mayor has repeatedly described the attacks as an attempt to shatter the country’s confidence and unity. In his telling, the response proved the opposite.

“The lesson of 9/11 is that America is truly exceptional,” Giuliani said. “We withstood the worst attack of our history, intended by our enemies to destroy us.

"Instead, it drew us closer and made us more united. Our love for freedom and one another has given us a strength that surprised even ourselves.”

That message became closely associated with Giuliani ’s public role after the attacks, when New York was dealing with mass casualties, widespread fear and an enormous emergency response.

Nearly 3,000 people were killed on September 11, 2001, and the anniversary remains a day of remembrance for victims, families, first responders and survivors.

Giuliani has long emphasized unity over fear

Giuliani has made the same point in other reflections on the attacks.

“The attacks of September 11th were intended to break our spirit,” he said. “Instead we have emerged stronger and more unified.”

He added that Americans showed a renewed commitment to “political, economic and religious freedom, the rule of law and respect for human life.”

That framing helped define the immediate aftermath of 9/11, when public attention centered on first responders, rescue workers and the sense of solidarity that emerged across the country.

It also explains why Giuliani ’s quote has continued to circulate on anniversaries of the attacks. Rather than focusing only on the moment of tragedy, it presents resilience itself as the lasting lesson.

The 9/11 legacy more complicated with time

The passage of 25 years has also brought renewed scrutiny of decisions made after the attacks.

New York City recently released a large collection of documents related to air quality and health risks in Lower Manhattan following the collapse of the World Trade Center .

Mayor Zohran Mamdani has argued that people became sick because they were wrongly assured that the air was safe. Giuliani , through spokesperson Ted Goodman , pushed back strongly against attempts to place responsibility on his administration.

Goodman said the terrorists behind the attacks were “100 percent responsible” for the suffering and illness that followed, while also pointing to assurances from the Environmental Protection Agency about air quality.

“It is a shame that Mayor Mamdani is now attempting to score cheap partisan political points by seeming to blame local officials who rushed to the scene, rather than radical Islam, for September 11,” Goodman said.

That dispute shows how the memory of 9/11 now includes both the extraordinary response to the attacks and difficult questions about the long-term consequences.

Giuliani ’s central message, however, has remained consistent. His argument is that the country’s strength wasn't proven by avoiding tragedy, but by how people responded when tragedy arrived.

articles.title: Is Patriot Day or 9/11 a federal holiday?
articles.standfirst: It is a fairly new commemorative day in the context
articles.summary: It is a fairly new commemorative day in the context
articles.body:
O ne of the most important days in the calendar for residents of the USA is here, which is Patriots Day .

It is celebrated each year on the 11th of September, marking the 9/11 terror attacks which led to many deaths and incredible amounts of damage to New York City.

In the immediate aftermath of the attacks, carried out by terrorists from Al-Qaeda, President George W. Bush proclaimed Friday, September 14, 2001, as a National Day of Prayer and Remembrance for the Victims of the Terrorist Attacks on September 11, 2001.

It is not actually classed as being a federal holiday in the United States. In 2021, then-State Assemb. Lawler sponsored legislation to make September 11 a state holiday, although the measure failed to gain enough support for passage.

"Thousands of families have faced the repercussions of that day, especially the families of those who worked tirelessly on the pile, trying to find survivors and helping other families find closure," Lawler said in a statement.

The September 11 attacks left nearly 3,000 dead in New York, Washington, D.C., and Shanksville, Pennsylvania, while thousands more, including first responders, have died in the past two decades of chronic health issues related to the toxic air and dust in lower Manhattan.

When did Patriots Day become a federal holiday?

Patriots Day is not currently a federal holiday but there are plenty of people that think it should be.

Rep. Anthony D'Esposito said: "I think that it's up to us as individuals; up to us as leaders and up to those who are educators to make people understand that this is a day where we're remembering and paying tribute.

"It's not a day off. It's not a mattress sale. It's not a day to get a discount on a car. It's a day to remember and honor the fallen who made that sacrifice on one of the worst attacks on American soil."

Patriot Day dedicated to honor first responders

While Patriot Day doesn't close down essential services, it remains a critical day of reflection for millions of Americans.

Many people participate in community service projects, attend candlelight vigils, or donate to organizations that support first responders and veterans.

The American flag is often flown at half-staff as a mark of respect, both at government buildings and private residences.

articles.title: Donald Trump's million-dollar gift to his assistant, Natalie Harp, is shaking the walls of the White House
articles.standfirst: Natalie Harp, Margo Martin, and Chamberlain Harris received a large sum of money
articles.summary: Natalie Harp, Margo Martin, and Chamberlain Harris received a large sum of money
articles.body:
The amounts appear in the financial disclosures of the three advisers, recently released by the U.S. Administration . In the documents, Donald Trump appears as the person who made the payments, described as a “cash gift for the holidays”.

The figure is especially striking because of its size. Each of the three aides receives an annual salary close to $150,000 for her work in the White House , so the money received as a gift is approximately equivalent to 30% of her annual salary.

Donald Trump gave a total of $135,000 in cash to three of his closest aides at the White House . The beneficiaries, Natalie Harp , Margo Martin and Chamberlain Harris, stated that they had each received $45,000 from the U.S. president, payments that have raised doubts among ethics experts about their possible legal standing.

Trump and the doubts about the legality of the payments: the “gift” amounts to 30% of their salaries

The payments have sparked controversy because U.S. federal legislation places restrictions on the additional compensation that public employees may receive beyond their official salary.

Natalie Harp , 35, is the best known of the three. Her closeness to Trump has on several occasions placed her at the center of media attention. Margo Martin , 31, works as a communications adviser and usually accompanies the president to record content for his social media.

The third beneficiary is Chamberlain Harris , 26, who serves as the executive assistant to the president and is also part of his innermost circle.

But those were not the only amounts handed over. According to information published by U.S. media, Trump also allegedly gave $20,000 to Walt Nauta, director of operations for the Oval Office and the president's former personal aide.

Experts consulted by the American press say they do not recall similar public precedents in which a president had handed such large amounts of cash to White House employees. A case that once again puts the internal practices of Trump’s closest circle under the spotlight.
